setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Philo Stomp"** (3 reviews): The jam starting about 8:55 into The Other One is singled out as a standout; The Philo jam is outstanding, with Phil leading in a nearly perfect way [9][13][15]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 other source): A tape flip occurs at 19:18 in this song [1]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The jam before the first verse is excellent, and the piece travels to some nice places [5]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-10-24.sonyecm250.unknown.miller.97614.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 25 songs; 204 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording quality is limited, but the performances win you over once your ears adjust; Vocals are distant and almost inaudible, and everything sounds extremely soft; hard to listen to; Audience tape quality is disappointing, especially the first set, which the reviewer doubts getting repeated listens [9][10][11]
- **gd72-10-24.pset2-sbd.hamilton.159.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 9 songs; 62 min; rated 2.67/5 by 6 [3]. Said about its sound: Levels run low and the board isn't the sharpest, but the mix is fairly good; A cut in the vocals loses the Spanish Lady section; The soundboard is a little rough [5][6][8][12]
- **gd1972-10-24.sbd.miller.106018.flac16**: soundboard; 7 songs; 62 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [4]
- **gd1972-10-24.sbd.gems.105842.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 61 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- The band never quite figured out the room's acoustics [8]
- The taper and friends kept quiet, with no chatter through the songs [10]
- Source covers set two, Truckin' through Johnny B. Goode; Deadbase and deadlists.com order the songs differently, and set one is reportedly unknown [3]
- Resembles the 10/18 show in its roughness and adventurous mood; the reviewer suggests the two belong together [6]
- Differs from other shows where Phil jams alone on his own muse [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-10-24.sonyecm250.unknown.miller.97614.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sony ECM-250 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-153/BASF Normal Bias 120 Min Tapes) [1]. Also: The reviewer would use this audience recording as a patch in The Other One; Unknown microphones to an unknown step to cassette; recorded by a legendary local taper; A cassette patch fills The Other One from 5:48 to 6:25; disc changes are seamless [1][11]
- **gd72-10-24.pset2-sbd.hamilton.159.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Taped by a prolific local Milwaukee taper on BASF 120 tapes, who rarely cut songs; reviewer obtained master copies; The soundboard covers only part of the second set, about sixty full minutes; Soundboard chain: master reel to one cassette, to DAT, then CDR copied twice [3][8][12]
- **gd1972-10-24.sbd.miller.106018.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD [4]. Also: The only soundboard source listed without a cassette generation; reel master came from David Gans; Patch sources were pitch corrected, and tracks are labeled to match the audience recording [4]
- **gd1972-10-24.sbd.gems.105842.flac16**: transferred by Jamie Waddell and Patrick White; source: SBD > Master Reel > ? > DAT [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Jerrybase: [Grateful Dead – 1972-10-24](https://jerrybase.com/events/19721024-01) [18]
- Photo by zoooma (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead 10/24/72 Milwaukee Performing Ar…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/zoooma/3054185798/) [19]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/zoooma/3054185798/) [20]
